sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "Mighty waters" through the Targum and Midrash, describing God's love for Israel and their protection from the nations.

translations.translation: Mighty waters*1
cannot quench the love, and rivers cannot wash it away; if a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, they would utterly despise him.
And it is explained in the Targum
(and in Midrash Rabbah*2
and Rashi),
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the children of Israel,
If all the nations of the world gather,
a multitude of many peoples like the roar of mighty waters,
they cannot quench
(G-d forbid)
the love between Me and Israel.
And if all the kings of the earth and their princes gather,
the mighty and numerous river waters,
they cannot erase
(G-d forbid)
you from the world.
If a man gives all the wealth of his house to acquire the Torah in exile,
I will repay him double in the World to Come, and all the plunder and spoil of the camp of Gog will be his.
We have a little sister, etc. At that time, the heavenly angels judged: one nation—this is Israel—is in the land, and she is small in merits;
what shall we do for our sister on the day when she is spoken of by the nations to go up to war against her?
And Michael, the prince of Israel, answered,
If she is a wall, etc.,
If this nation stands like a wall among the nations, not intermarrying with them,
for if she holds fast to her faith and fear to acquire the unity of His blessed Name, we will be a fortress for her, and the nations will have no power to rule over her,

And if she is a door, etc., and even if she is impoverished in mitzvos, we will seek mercy for her before Hashem, and He will remember for her the merit of the Torah of the schoolchildren, which is written on the tablets of their hearts.
And in the Midrash it concludes,
The nations of the world say: We sin, and Israel does not sin
(in astonishment),

We have a little sister. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: Just as with this little girl, when she is small and sins against her parents, her parents do not complain against her because she is small,
so too are Israel,

And it concludes: But against your will you will be Mine, as it is said, "You will not be what you say, 'We will be like the nations,' etc." Rather, what will I do? With a strong hand, etc., I will reign over you.
From this you learn the belovedness of Israel before the Omnipresent.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section reconciles the two interpretations of "mighty waters"—the mystical one of divine contemplation and the simple one of Israel's lowly state—showing they are complementary.

translations.translation: B)
And it is necessary to understand how this explanation fits with the explanation of our Rebbe on this portion regarding the verse "mighty waters,"
And it is based on what is written in the Zohar,
That "mighty waters" refers to the contemplation one contemplates on the greatness of Hashem, that He fills all worlds and encompasses all worlds, and everything before Him is considered as nothing,
Which is the contemplation of "Shema Yisrael" and "Baruch Shem,"

From which is drawn "And you shall love" with all your heart, etc., until one reaches the level of "with all your might" without limit, and he cannot quiet and quench the thirst of this love through the mighty waters themselves, which are the contemplation and knowledge, and even not through the comprehensions of Gan Eden,
And rivers cannot wash it away,
For "rivers" refers to the revelation in Gan Eden, as it is written, "And a river goes out*3
from Eden to water the garden,"
For although the revelation in Gan Eden is a revelation of a most exalted light, and there are countless types of levels within it,
For even though in general only the Lower Gan Eden and the Upper Gan Eden are mentioned in the books, our sages of blessed memory said,*4
"Torah scholars have no rest, etc., as it is said, 'They go from strength to strength,' etc." Nevertheless, "rivers cannot wash it away,"
For all the revelation of light in Gan Eden cannot satisfy the thirst,
Only specifically through Torah and mitzvos,
About which it says,
"If a man gives all the wealth of his house for love,"
"A man" refers to the Holy One, blessed be He,
When He gives all the wealth of His house,
That is the Torah and mitzvos,
Behold, "they would utterly despise him" — a term of plunder and spoil,
Like the plundering of precious treasures that one plunders and snatches due to his great desire for it,
And as our sages of blessed memory said,*5
"In this world from which we depart, snatch and eat, snatch and drink,"
For specifically through Torah and mitzvos can one satisfy the thirst,
For they are above the level of a river,
Rather, they are the level of a wellspring,
"And she went down to the wellspring and filled her pitcher" — the twenty-four books of the Torah,
Which will be revealed in the future, as it is written, "And a wellspring will go out from the House of Hashem," etc.,
But although this is not in revelation, this level is actually drawn down now through Torah and practical mitzvos,
And therefore, specifically through this will one satisfy the thirst.

For according to this explanation, the verse explains the level of Israel, that they are on a most exalted level, and their love for G-dliness is so powerful that even the most sublime revelations cannot satisfy their thirst,
And according to the explanation of the Targum and Midrash, the verse speaks when Israel is in the lowest state,
"We have a little sister,"
Small in merits, and they sin, to the point that the nations of the world want to equate themselves with Israel.
And in truth, these two explanations are not only not contradictory, but they actually support and explain each other.
